title: Skill or Skip? Learning Selective Skill Invocation in Agentic Tasks via Dual-Granularity Preference Learning
abstract: arXiv:2606.00510v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Agent skills are callable procedural modules that provide reusable knowledge and execution policies for complex agentic tasks. However, existing methods mainly focus on selecting relevant skills or improving the skills themselves, while overlooking whether a relevant skill should actually be invoked at the current decision point. Unhelpful invocations may introduce irrelevant context and disrupt an otherwise correct execution process. To address this issue, we propose SelSkill, a dual-granularity preference-learning framework for selective skill invocation. SelSkill formulates skill use as a skill-or-skip decision, uses predictive uncertainty to prioritize candidate decision points, and constructs controlled invoke-skip preference pairs from shared trajectory prefixes. It further combines episode-level outcome preferences with step-level invocation preferences to capture both overall trajectory quality and the local effectivene

translated_title: 技能还是跳过？通过双粒度偏好学习在智能体任务中学习选择性技能调用
translated_abstract: 智能体技能是可调用的程序化模块，为复杂的智能体任务提供可复用的知识和执行策略。然而，现有方法主要关注选择相关技能或改进技能本身，而忽视了相关技能是否真的应该在当前决策点被调用。无益的调用可能引入无关的上下文，破坏原本正确的执行过程。为了解决这一问题，我们提出了SelSkill，一个用于选择性技能调用的双粒度偏好学习框架。SelSkill将技能使用表述为“调用或跳过”的决策，利用预测不确定性对候选决策点进行优先排序，并从共享的轨迹前缀构建受控的调用-跳过偏好对。它进一步将回合级的结果偏好与步骤级的调用偏好相结合，以同时捕捉整体轨迹质量和局部有效性。
tldr: 该论文提出SelSkill框架，将技能使用建模为“调用或跳过”的决策，通过结合回合级结果偏好与步骤级调用偏好的双粒度偏好学习，实现智能体任务中技能的选择性调用，避免无益的技能调用破坏原本正确的执行过程。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes SelSkill, a dual-granularity preference-learning framework that formulates skill use as a skill-or-skip decision, combining episode-level outcome preferences with step-level invocation preferences to enable selective skill invocation and prevent unhelpful invocations from disrupting otherwise correct execution in agentic tasks.
